content.body:
A very advanced single-engine fighter design by 1940 standards, the Spitfire is certainly one of the most famous fighter planes of all time. Elegant and sleek with the famous elliptical wings, it was a dogfighter's dream in low wing-stressed metal monoplane designs. Fast and maneuverable, its only serious rival at the time was the Luftwaffe's Bf 109.
However, the Mk I suffered from comparatively weak armament and fuel starvation to the engine when under negative G forces. These weak spots were all that held the Mk I back in its early deployments. As the Mk Ia's power and armament were added in later versions, it truly fulfilled its design goals staying fast, climbing quickly, turning tightly and bringing decent firepower to bear on its opponents.
